questions.text:
Let A be nxn real valued square symmetric matrix of rank 2 with [latex]\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}A^{2}_{ij}=50[/latex]. Consider the following statements.

(I) One eigen value must be in [-5, 5]
(II) The eigen value with the largest magnitude must be strictly greater than 5.

Which of the above statements about eigen values of A is/are necessarily CORRECT?
questions.solution:
A is symmetric with rank 2, so it has two non-zero eigenvalues [latex]\lambda_1,\lambda_2[/latex] (the rest are 0), and [latex]\sum A_{ij}^2=\lambda_1^2+\lambda_2^2=50[/latex].

- (I): [latex]\lambda_1^2+\lambda_2^2=50[/latex] forces one of them to have [latex]|\lambda|\le5[/latex] (and the zero eigenvalues are in [[latex]-[/latex]5, 5] anyway) True
- (II): [latex]\lambda_1=\lambda_2=5[/latex] gives 50, and the largest is not strictly greater than 5 False

Answer: (I) only

questions.text:
A computer network uses polynomials over GF(2) for error checking with 8 bits as
information bits and uses [latex]x^{3}+x+1[/latex] as the generator polynomial to generate the check bits. In
this network, the message 01011011 is transmitted as
questions.solution:
Generator [latex]x^3+x+1[/latex] = 1011. Append 3 zeros to 01011011 and divide: 01011011000 [latex]\div[/latex] 1011 leaves remainder 101.

Transmitted = 01011011 101

Answer: 01011011101

questions.text:
Consider a combination of T and D flip-flops connected as shown below. The output of the D flip-flop is connected to the input of the T flip-flop and the output of the T flip-flop is connected to the input of the D flip-flop

Initailly, both [latex]Q_{0}[/latex] and [latex]Q_{1}[/latex] are set to 1 (before the 1st clock cycle). The outputs
questions.solution:
T input = [latex]Q_0[/latex], D input = [latex]Q_1[/latex]. So [latex]Q_1^+=Q_1\oplus Q_0[/latex] and [latex]Q_0^+=Q_1[/latex]. Start [latex]Q_1Q_0[/latex] = 11:
- cycle 1: 01
- cycle 2: 10
- cycle 3: 11
- cycle 4: 01

Answer: 11 after the 3rd cycle and 01 after the 4th cycle

questions.text:
If G is grammar with productions
[latex]S\rightarrow SaS|aSb|bSa|SS|\epsilon[/latex]
where S is the start variable, then which one of the following is not generated by G?
questions.solution:
Each rule adds a's and b's in a way that never gives more b's than a's: aSb and bSa add one of each, SaS adds an extra a, SS and [latex]\epsilon[/latex] add nothing. So every generated string has [latex]\#a\ge\#b[/latex].

babba has 2 a's and 3 b's [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] cannot be generated.

Answer: babba
